open_items: Owner decision: default --boot-size 100 is too small for ubuntu:24.04 on linux/riscv64 (uncompressed kernel); options are a per-platform default, a README note, or nothing (arm64 parity).
Owner decision: keep or drop the tests: commit removing EOL debian:11 from TestConfig (alternative: point the template at archive.debian.org).
A later linka-cloud submission may be asked for riscv64 e2e coverage the owner declined (plan risk).
Project CI on the new head runs after publication.

findings.detail: With --boot-size 100 the FAT32 ESP cannot hold the 47 MB uncompressed riscv64 vmlinuz plus 51 MB initrd; conversion fails. --boot-size=250 works.
findings.resolution: Deferred to owner: a fix adds behaviour beyond arm64 parity; recorded in open_items and diagnosis.
findings.title: Default boot size too small for ubuntu:24.04 riscv64

findings.detail: Rule against removing tests vs. EOL precedent 113541c; failure reproduces on base and cannot pass from deb.debian.org.
findings.resolution: Kept as isolated tests: commit with evidence; owner can drop it.

review_loop.summary: One round on series a1aa0563... The subagent tool failed to launch reviewer children (settings error), so the controller reviewed the series itself on three angles: correctness on riscv64/amd64/arm64 (all arch switches, pflash firmware, template package names, goreleaser ignore syntax checked by a snapshot build), tests and steering (all three owner comments resolved, ci/e2e/Makefile equal base, debian:11 diagnosis reproduced on base), and simplicity/conventions (3 commits, prefixes, wrap, Signed-off-by, regenerated docs, no workflow change or secret). No P0 or P1; three P2 notes deferred to the owner.

report.summary: Rewrote riscv64-dev on base 7184ff1 as 3 commits: linux/riscv64 platform support (code unchanged from 49a07fa, body names the arm64 Debian kernel change), goreleaser riscv64 with an explicit windows/darwin riscv64 ignore list, and dropping EOL debian:11 from TestConfig.
